claims.text: PtMo nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon will show enhanced HER activity compared with standard commercial Pt catalysts.
PtMo nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon will show enhanced HOR activity compared with standard commercial Pt catalysts.
PtMo nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon will be more durable than standard commercial Pt catalysts during HER and HOR operation.
Standard commercial Pt catalysts typically consist of pure Pt nanoparticles on carbon supports.
The proposed synthesis will form a well-alloyed PtMo phase.
The PtMo phase will be nanoscale-dispersed on a high-surface-area nitrogen-doped carbon support.
Incorporating Mo electronically modifies the Pt surface.
Mo-induced electronic modification tunes the hydrogen adsorption free energy on Pt.
Tuning hydrogen adsorption free energy facilitates HER and HOR kinetics.
Improved support–particle interactions stabilize the PtMo nanoparticles under operating conditions.
Nanoparticle stabilization by nitrogen-doped carbon enhances catalyst durability.
PtMo on nitrogen-doped carbon will have lower HER and HOR overpotentials than pure Pt on carbon.
PtMo on nitrogen-doped carbon will produce higher HER and HOR current densities than pure Pt on carbon.
PtMo on nitrogen-doped carbon will exhibit less activity loss during extended cycling than pure Pt on carbon.
The proposed enhancements are expected under acidic electrolyte conditions.
The catalyst's effects may differ in alkaline environments.
The catalyst's effects may differ at extreme operating temperatures.
The magnitude of performance improvement and the optimal Pt:Mo ratio depend on synthesis conditions and particle dispersion.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline uses pure Pt nanoparticles on undoped carbon, whereas the falsification experiment compares PtMo/N-doped carbon with pure Pt on the same carbon support, implying an N-doped support. These are different controls and would test different contributions from Mo alloying and nitrogen doping.
